quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Don't brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
Brake the front tire too hard and don't brake the rear tire hard enough.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes don't brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.

questions.question: The center of a lane:

options.text: Is always the best place to ride a motorcycle.
Has oil and grease, but is usually safe to ride on.
Has oil and grease, and is never safe to ride on.
Is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has oil and grease, but is usually safe to ride on.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of each lane. This area is usually safe to ride on unless the road is wet. You should still avoid large buildup of oil and grease at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: When a group exits a highway, what riding formation should be used?

options.text: Staggered
Single-file
Paired up
Riding three across a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, a group should switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Always stay in the left part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Always stay in the right part of the lane throughout the entire curve.
Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change anytime. Be prepared to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not follow the road's curve.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.
Always ride in the right part of the lane.
Be flexible and consider many different factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and consider many different factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Any part of the lane can work. Choose your position so that other drivers can see you and you have space around you.

questions.question: When the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left part of a lane.
The center of the lane.
The right part of the lane.
All parts of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in a strip down the center of a lane. This strip is usually safe to ride on, except when the road is wet. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to its side and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, a good idea is to:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center strip of a lane is dangerous when wet because of oil deposits. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. It is also best to slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about hazards and road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars look closer than they really are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars look farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances in convex mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is never safe for motorcyclists.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided because other parts of the lane do not have oil.
Improves traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area gives enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. You need extra distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see the road ahead, or if traffic is heavy and other drivers might cut in front of you.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Swerve and not brake, using only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: The best way to get maximum braking in a straight line is by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If the road requires a longer stopping distance than normal, you should:

options.text: Decrease your usual following distance.
Increase your usual following distance.
Travel on the shoulder.
Ask someone else to ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your usual following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. This includes slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Keep at least a three-second following distance.

questions.question: The right footwear for riding a motorcycle should have:

options.text: Long, loose laces.
Short heels.
Tall heels.
Always be sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal.
Start slowing earlier than normal.
Increase your following distance.
Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger's extra weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: The center of a lane usually has an oily strip. This part of the lane is:

options.text: Never safe for motorcyclists.
Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area gives enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and avoid moving around so the driver can focus on riding. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How much alcohol was consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.
